payload.overall_summary: The student demonstrates strong foundational communication skills, including appropriate greeting, active listening, logical information gathering, and clear delivery of treatment instructions. They build rapport effectively and provide relevant, accurate advice. However, the consultation is hindered by rapid pacing, limited use of confirmatory techniques like teach-back or summarising, and minimal adaptation to the patient's potential health literacy or engagement needs. Nonverbal behaviours could not be assessed from audio, but verbal expressiveness appears flat. With improvements in pacing, interaction, and verification, the communication would be more patient-centred and effective.

criteria.label: Elicits that area around the patienAND other symptoms of tinea (there is cracking, redness and peeling of skin between toes) (i.e. when asked to describe symptoms)
criteria.reason: The student asked if there are any other unusual symptoms like fever or swelling, but did not elicit or confirm the specific symptoms of cracking, redness, and peeling skin between the toes as described by the patient.

criteria.label: Elicits that symptoms started three weeks ago after working on the farm wearing boots all day (i.e. when asked when it started)
criteria.reason: The student confirmed the duration of symptoms as three weeks but did not elicit that the symptoms started after working on the farm wearing boots all day.

criteria.label: Elicits the patient has not had the symptoms before AND has not tried anything for symptoms yet AND has no signs of infection (no pus, swelling etc.)
criteria.reason: The student did not elicit whether the patient has had similar symptoms before; they only confirmed no current medications and no allergies.

criteria.label: Advises patient has tinea OR fungal infection on the skin OR cause of itchiness due to wearing boots whole day (hot and humid)
criteria.reason: The student advised that the symptoms are consistent with tinea (referred to as 'tin of patties') and attributed the cause to wearing boots creating a humid environment for fungus to grow.

criteria.label: Recommends any of ONE the following topical therapy: Terbinafine, OR Miconazole/ clotrimazole/ econazole/ bifonazole/ ketoconazole, OR Combination hydrocortisone/antifungal
criteria.reason: The student recommended a 1% terbinafine cream, which is one of the specified topical therapies.

criteria.label: Counsels on how to use chosen product in Point 5: - Terbinafine: Apply a thin layer once daily for 1 week - Miconazole: Apply a thin layer twice daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Clotrimazole/Econazole: Apply a thin layer 2 or 3 times a day; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Bifonazole: Apply a thin layer once daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Ketoconazole: Apply a thin layer 1 or 2 times daily; continue for 2 weeks after symptoms resolve - Combination hydrocortisone/antifungal (available combinations are clotrimazole + hydrocortisone OR miconazole + hydrocortisone): Apply a thin layer 2 times a day for one week then continue with antifungal only
criteria.reason: The student counselled to apply the terbinafine cream once daily for 7 days, matching the recommended usage for terbinafine.

criteria.label: Recommends at least ONE of the following future preventive action: maintain good foot hygiene; keep feet clean and dry especially after working at the farm; avoid sharing towels/footwear; use antifungal (or non-medicated) powder in shoes to reduce moisture; wear open-toed footwear; use cotton (non-synthetic) socks; wear shoes that have breathable material (such as leather); place shoes in the sun to dry if it get damp; discard old shoes that may have a high density of fungal spores
criteria.reason: The student recommended avoiding occlusive footwear and using a separate towel not to be shared with others, which aligns with preventive actions like avoiding shared towels and keeping feet dry.

criteria.label: Advises the patient to see their doctor /pharmacist if their symptoms do not improve or worsens
criteria.reason: The student advised the patient to visit the doctor immediately if symptoms worsen or do not resolve after one week of treatment.

keep_start_stop.keep: You appropriately recommended terbinafine cream and provided clear instructions on its use, including duration and application. You also gave relevant preventive advice such as avoiding shared towels and non-occlusive footwear, and advised timely follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen.
keep_start_stop.start: You should begin consultations by actively eliciting the full symptom description, including cracking, redness, and peeling between the toes, and explore potential contributing factors such as farm work and boot use. Additionally, explicitly ask about prior history of similar symptoms to confirm this is a new presentation.
keep_start_stop.stop: Avoid using unclear or incorrect terminology such as 'tin of patties' when explaining tinea to the patient; use accurate and professional language like 'fungal infection' or 'tinea' to ensure clarity and avoid confusion.

payload.overall_summary: The student demonstrated strengths in recommending appropriate antifungal therapy, providing correct usage instructions, offering preventive advice, and advising follow-up care. However, key gaps in history-taking were observed, including failure to elicit specific symptoms (cracking, redness, peeling), the link between symptoms and farm/boot use, and absence of prior symptom history. Addressing these gaps will improve diagnostic accuracy and patient-centred care.
